summary: 1934 L-4 ground-house lookout on Burley Mountain in Gifford Pinchot NF, Lewis County, WA; staffed until 1974, now day use and fire detection, with a restoration aimed at rental.

facts.design: L-4 ground house, 14 by 14 feet, no catwalk

staffing.status: staffed until 1974 (National Forest Foundation); 2026 Forest Service page says still used for fire detection

access.note: Day use only, from sunrise to sunset, per the Forest Service page last updated August 24, 2026. A restoration to allow public rental is planned; no rental was found open.

visit.trail_note: Half-mile trail No. 256A from a parking area in the saddle below the summit; the Forest Service recommends parking near the gate and walking the last 300 feet

events.note: Chehalis Bee-Nugget notice said K.I. Peters would occupy Burley Mountain for the summer
June 1931 notice places K.I. Peters at Burley Mountain on the Randle district
L-4 ground house constructed; the register and the Forest Service both give 1934
Daily Chronicle notice of May 27, 1960 calls Burley the first lookout in the Randle District, scheduled to open June 24. This does not square with the 1930-31 notices
May 1964 announcement: the 37 regular and emergency lookouts would be cut to six regularly manned ones; Burley Mountain was one of the six retained, mainly for communications
Summer 1968 staffed by a Concrete, Washington, teacher named Darleen Kemper in one Daily Chronicle story and Charleen Kemper in another
Jan Grose, 23, of Mossyrock, operated the lookout, the only tower open in the Randle Ranger District; officials said better radio coverage would make it unnecessary
Staffed until 1974 per the National Forest Foundation
Registered November 4, 2000 as US 356, WA 37; nominated by Ray Kresek
Forest Service page (updated August 24, 2026): one of three remaining lookouts on the forest, still used for fire detection, day use only

corrections.why: The register describes a 14-by-14-foot ground house with no catwalk, not a tower, and no source read gives a height for the structure. 94.5 m does not match the structure described.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: An undated firelookout.com listing says the cab has not been used for many years. The Forest Service page, updated August 24, 2026, says it is still used for fire detection. The newer Forest Service page is treated as current, so the lookout is recorded as standing and in occasional use.

notes_for_editor: Record height_m 94.5 is wrong for a ground house; correction proposed (omit). Elevation differs by source: register 5,154 ft (record 1570.9 m matches it); National Forest Foundation and the 1968 newspaper say about 5,310 ft; firelookout.com says 5304. Not reconciled. Staffing: the 1930 and 1931 K.I. Peters notices conflict with the May 1960 notice calling Burley the first lookout in the Randle District; not reconciled. The 1968 name is Darleen in one Daily Chronicle story and Charleen in another; unresolved. Distance: the 1960 notice says 28 miles south of Randle, firelookout.com says 10 miles SSE; the record coordinates match the register. A search snippet (TrailChick) suggests a tent camp in 1930 before the 1934 cab; I did not open that page, so it is unverified. The National Forest Foundation article is undated; its two-year restoration timeline may be out of date, and no rental was found open. Status: standing is supported by the 2026 Forest Service page. Page reads used: 6. WebSearch used: 1.
